touches.text: Logging and diagnostics. These can be in different files, mixed in together.
The base classes all inherit from base, and so bring its logging, diagnostics and core patterns with them:
base shim: the base class for every shim, customized for the device it interfaces with, internal or external.
build_inspector: python sieves run after a build; reds a component that fails one (no charter, no proofs, a silent device, ...). "We find a new thing, we add a new sieve." → CodeMother (10.3.5)
diagnostic_inspector: the smart reader of the dumb breadcrumbs base's logging leaves; complete diagnosis on the first pass. → CodeMother? [Q#40: or base, since it reads base's logs?]

Owns the inspectors and gates (draft, moving from standalone): build_inspector, plan_inspector, diagnostic_inspector, ticket_inspector, corrosion, exemptions, rehearsal, determinism, import_sieve. The code pipeline's inspectors and gates move to CodeMother; any that are not about code (if such existed) would not. (Q#31, Akien 2026-10-27)

ROOT INTENTION for checks and gates (Akien, 2026-10-27): the inspector does all the checks, so there is no need for more checks anywhere else. The inspector's output is consumed by the gate. The gate's output is the certificate. "This was how I meant it all along."
